name: Question-answering computer
definition: A computer holding broad knowledge that answers arbitrary factual questions put to it in ordinary language.
what: MIT's START went online on the Internet in 1993 and answered English questions from the public on many topics (Boris Katz)
fit: A publicly reachable computer answering ordinary-language factual questions on many topics, used by outside people for that purpose; knowledge is hand-annotated so breadth is limited.

sources.title: Boris Katz
sources.quote: Boris Katz is the creator of the START information processing system (since 1993 - on the Internet)

note: Kept from the second pass. No earlier deployed open-domain question answerer was found (Protosynthex was a research system). Ask Jeeves 1996 is later and matched questions to pages. No contemporary 1993-1995 source found in ia_search3.

name: Three-dimensional holographic display
definition: A display that shows images, maps or people as volumetric three-dimensional pictures viewable from several sides.
what: The Actuality Systems Perspecta Spatial 3D volumetric display was integrated with a clinical radiation-therapy planning system (Pinnacle) so that planners could view patient anatomy and beams in 3D from any side.
fit: A swept-volume display showing changing patient-derived 3-D images in a 25 cm volume viewable from any side, used for its real purpose in treatment planning.

sources.publisher: Journal of Applied Clinical Medical Physics (PMC)
sources.title: Application of a 3D volumetric display for radiation therapy treatment planning I: quality assurance procedures
sources.quote: volume that is viewable from any side, floating within a translucent dome

sources.publisher: Journal of Applied Clinical Medical Physics (PMC)
sources.title: Application of a 3D volumetric display for radiation therapy treatment planning I: quality assurance procedures
sources.quote: has been integrated with the Pinnacle TPS (Philips Medical Systems, Madison WI), for treatment planning

note: Replaces second pass 1972 (Cross's moving multiplex hologram, an art/exhibit piece). The date is that of the clinical paper; a web search suggests the first Perspecta was delivered to the NIH Clinical Center in January 2004 (AuntMinnie, host blocked) and 2002 sales to universities for research, so real use probably began about 2002-2004, but I could not fetch a dated source. No earlier use outside the lab found for ITT's 1960 rotating-screen display (only a working model) or Withey's Peritron. Zebra Imaging's printed holographic maps for the US military are static, so excluded.

name: Automatic dictation transcription
definition: A machine that listens to dictation and produces the written or typed text automatically.
what: Kurzweil Applied Intelligence officially released its 1,000-word Voicerad system in Boston in December 1986; a radiologist was already writing his reports with it by voice. Dragon Systems had announced Voicescribe-1000 'automatic dictation transcription system' in June 1986.
fit: A computer listens to a user's spoken dictation of reports and produces the edited, printed text, used by a working radiologist.

sources.title: Voice system cures MD ills
sources.quote: allows radiologists to dictate, edit and print out diagnostic X-ray reports by voice

sources.title: Speech transcriber announced
sources.quote: announced Voicescribe-1000, an automatic dictation transcription system

note: Replaces Dragon Dictate 1990 in the second pass: Kurzweil Voicerad and Dragon Voicescribe-1000 were dictation products in 1986 (PC Magazine 27 Oct 1987 also lists both). Earlier: Threshold Technology voice input from 1972 was data entry of commands, not dictation; Kurzweil 1985 Voice Report not found in searches. Voicescribe-1000 was only announced in June 1986 (availability not shown), so Voicerad December 1986 is the first documented in use. Limited vocabulary and discrete speech, so a strict dictation fit but narrow.

name: Companion or sex robot
definition: A robot built to provide companionship, affection, romance or sex.
what: Furby went on general sale in the United States (launched 2 October 1998, with a press event at FAO Schwarz, New York), selling 1.8 million in 1998.
fit: The robotic pet toy was bought and kept by ordinary families as a companion that responds to touch and sound.

sources.publisher: Mary Beth's Beanie World: Furby Edition
sources.title: Mary Beth's Beanie World: Furby Edition
sources.quote: for his grand arrival at the flagship FAO Schwarz store in early October

sources.title: Furby
sources.quote: The product officially launched on October 2, 1998

note: Replaces second pass 1999-06-01 (AIBO sale; Sony's robot dog went on sale 1999-06-01, 3,000 units in Japan sold out in 20 minutes per a 1999-06-04 news item) because Furby was on sale eight months earlier. Same fit caveat as the demonstration. Paro handmade sales from 2004 are later.

name: Central computer directing many robots
definition: A single computer or master robot that coordinates and directs a whole population of robots.
what: Volvo Kalmar assembly plant in regular production use of its fleet of computer-guided carriers.
fit: The plant's fleet of computer-guided carriers did its production work, and all of them could be directed from one central computer.

sources.title: Architecture Plus, November 12, 1974
sources.quote: forms of "carriers," battery-powered and computer-guided, that creep silently about the factory bearing body assemblies

sources.title: Volvo
sources.quote: carriers at Kalmar can be controlled from a central data computer which is the heart and brain of the factory

note: Same event as the demonstration, so same date. Replaces Walgreens/Kiva 2007. Fit is partial (computer-guided fleet; central control inferred).

name: Automated face recognition
definition: Cameras and computers that identify people by matching their faces against stored images.
what: By 1994 facial-recognition biometric products had reached the marketplace (access control); the DMV offices of West Virginia and New Mexico followed, using automated face recognition against duplicate licences after the 1993 FERET test.
fit: Commercial systems used cameras and computers to match a person's face against an enrolled stored image for entry control and identity checks.

sources.title: Biometric Identification Verification Technology Status and Feasibility Study
sources.quote: Systems which have reached the marketplace include fingerprint, thumbprint, hand geometry, keystroke dynamics, signature dynamics, voice patterns, retina patterns, and facial recognition.

sources.title: Facial recognition system
sources.quote: became the first DMV offices to use automated facial recognition systems to prevent people from obtaining multiple driving licenses

note: Replaces second pass 1997 (ZN-Face sale). The 1994 DTIC study says facial recognition products were already on the market but names no deployment and calls them unreliable (it judged them unable to meet DoD needs), so the date is the earliest documented market presence, not a documented first user. The DMV use (West Virginia, New Mexico) is after 1993 but I found no dated source. Mexico 2000 and Super Bowl 2001 are later.

name: Sleep learning
definition: Teaching people while they sleep or are hypnotized by playing recorded lessons.
what: Zust et al. (University of Bern) played recorded pseudoword/German word pairs to young adults in slow-wave sleep and found they had formed and kept new word associations that showed up on an implicit test after waking.
fit: Recorded vocabulary was played to sleeping people and they retained new verbal associations from it, so teaching by recorded sound during sleep worked, though only for implicit word-pair associations and not for general lessons.

sources.title: Implicit Vocabulary Learning during Sleep Is Bound to Slow-Wave Peaks
sources.quote: While in slow-wave sleep during a nap, a series of word pairs comprising pseudowords, e.g., "tofer," and actual German words, e.g., "Haus" (house), were played

note: Second pass gave nothing. This is the earliest strictly fitting result I found. Rejected: Saliger's Psycho-Phone (1927, patented 1932, sold as a sleep-teaching phonograph) and 1950s-60s commercial sleep-learning records, because there was no evidence they worked (the Wikipedia history says Emmons and Simon's 1956 EEG studies found material presented during sleep was not recalled and called it 'impractical and probably impossible'); Arzi et al. 2012 (Nature Neuroscience, 'Humans can learn new information during sleep') showed learning of tone-odour associations in sleep, which is conditioning rather than teaching with lessons, so earlier but a loose analogue; Schreiner and Rasch 2015 only cued words learned while awake. Hypnosis tapes: no controlled evidence found. The abstract itself says earlier evidence 'is inconclusive'. Hence low confidence.
